input.summary:
Entrance hall lamps written at the end of room-1.mjs: three standing lanterns at (45,4,43), (50,4,46), (47,4,56), off the designer's footprint. In a scratch build where the interior air is unclaimed they light the hall to min 8 with 0 dark cells, and the stair foot reads 8+ with no hidden light.
The real build is still dark: 71 dark cells, and runParts refuses all three lanterns because shell.mjs box() fills each room with "air", which claims the interior.
The fix belongs to the shell part and is not applied (outside my file): build only the four wall faces so the room air stays unclaimed.
left: Real build.nbt entrance hall is still dark: 71 of 104 floor cells at light 0, runParts reports refused:3 for room: entrance hall (lanterns at 45,4,43 / 50,4,46 / 47,4,56). Blocker is parts/shell.mjs box(): fill([x0+1,3,z0+1],[x1-1,17,z1-1],"air") claims the room air. Shell owner must build only the four wall faces (tested in /tmp/lamp-scratch: faces-only shell, same lamps -> min 8, 0 dark, room walk ok). Not applied: shell.mjs is another part's file.

The designer's furniture (layers() rows and centre chain lanterns in room-1) is commented out for the same reason; once the shell is fixed it can be re-enabled. Its footprint (settees x45/x50 z49..50, console planks at 45,4,44 and 50,4,44, coat rack x50 z43..44, lamp posts 45,4,48 / 50,4,56 / 49,4,59) was kept clear of my lantern cells.

Designer's stair concern resolved: with the designer's own lamp layout the four cells x45..46 z56..57 read 6-7 (scratch); with the lantern at 47,4,56 they read 8+. No hidden light is needed, and light blocks are not survival-valid anyway.

stairs.mjs builds no rail along the flight: birch_fence sits only at x47 y11 on the upper floor, so the flight's open side has nothing to hide a light under. The designer's note assumes a rail that doesn't exist yet (stair joiner's call).
FIT still reports 'hallway to nowhere' at 45,6,59 (the back of the hall, z59..60 dead end). That is a shell/stair layout issue, not a lighting one, and it is not changed here.

waste.what: Checked whether runParts refuses a light placed in the room's air by building a one-lantern probe and reading parts-report.json, then restoring the file.
waste.cost: 2 full make.sh runs and a probe edit/restore; about 4 tool calls
waste.tool: mcd room / mcd light should flag cells already claimed by an earlier part (e.g. 'claimed: shell air, refused for later parts') and the runParts report should name the claiming part per cell, so a lamplighter sees the lock before probing.

waste.what: The LAMPS suggestions in mcd room include cells that are not placeable (e.g. 50,4,50 sits on the designer's east settee footprint and on shell-claimed air).
waste.cost: one wrong candidate tested, then a hand search for alternative cells against the designer's layers() rows (about 6 cell checks)
waste.tool: mcd room --lamps should filter candidates to unclaimed air, self-supported cells, and cells outside any designer footprint, or accept a --avoid layers.json.

waste.what: Evaluated lamp sets by hand-editing room-1.mjs and rebuilding the whole grid once per candidate (7-8 full builds, including one env-var switch per variant).
waste.cost: about 8 full builds plus file rewrites in a scratch copy
waste.tool: mcd light --add x,y,z:lantern(standing|hanging) on an existing build.nbt (a hypothetical lamp set, no rebuild) with the walk and fit checks it implies.

waste.what: Tested the shell fix by copying the whole build directory to /tmp and hand-editing parts/shell.mjs there to see whether unclaiming the interior lights the room.
waste.cost: one scratch copy, two failed shell edits (the first also removed the hollowing, so the hall was all wall), then a faces-only edit
waste.tool: runParts --unclaim-dry-run <part> (report which cells the part would free and what the room would become) would have answered this without editing a shell.

waste.what: Derived by hand which room cells the designer's furniture occupies at each height (from the layers() rows and the z/x offsets).
waste.tool: mcd plan (already prints the floor grid) should also print each layers() block's occupied cells per y, so footprints can be compared with a lamp set directly.
